craft_claim: Reflective writing stages emotion at a remove in time and attention — the event is past, the thinking is present — so the then-scene/now-reflection tense split is the tone's audible signature and its chief structural defense against both immersion and nostalgia.

supporting_evidence.location: 1800 Preface to Lyrical Ballads, definition of poetry and the account of composition
supporting_evidence.note: Wordsworth defines poetic composition as emotion whose origin is being 'recollected in tranquillity' — distance in time and attentional calm presented as the mechanism by which experience becomes art, not as its ornament. (Public-domain phrase, 1800 text.)

supporting_evidence.location: Whole poem: the dated revisits and the narration of what each visit gave the poet then versus now
supporting_evidence.note: The poem builds on an explicit then/now structure (a first visit in youth, a return years later) and tracks the changed meaning of each — the reflective tense-split in its canonical poetic form, with earlier selves corrected rather than idealized.

counterevidence.note: The same distance-in-time structure can slide into idealization of the earlier self or era — the nostalgic use. Distance is necessary for reflection but does not guarantee non-idealization; the boundary against tone-nostalgic is held by present-tense evaluation, not by the pastness of the material.

scope: Reflective passages in poetry, essay, memoir, and fiction; the tense signature is cross-form, with acknowledged variants below.
exceptions: Diary and journal entries stage reflection in the same 'now' as the entry's day; distance is supplied by address and evaluation instead of elapsed time.
Present-tense stream-of-consciousness can reflect in-scene; then the distance is psychic rather than temporal.
